# Alert Handler Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The alert handler is a bus-accessible security peripheral that gathers alert events from multiple on-chip alert sources, converts them into class-based interrupts, and can escalate unhandled interrupts into hardware escalation actions. It also performs continuous liveness and signal-integrity monitoring of the alert and escalation signaling paths.

The module shall:

- Provide four interrupt classes: class A, B, C, and D.
- Provide four escalation severity outputs.
- Support a compile-time configured number of alert sources.
- Allow software to configure which alert sources are enabled and into which class an event is classified.
- Record the cause of each interrupt so software can identify which alert source triggered a class interrupt.
- Provide programmable escalation behavior per class, including accumulation thresholds, interrupt timeouts, escalation phases, and phase-to-severity mapping.
- Perform randomized liveness checks on alert and escalation paths after configuration is locked.
- Detect invalid differential signaling and missing or unexpected responses, and report them as local alert events.
- Provide a crashdump output that exposes current state and status information without requiring bus access.

## 2. Reset and Initialization Behavior

After reset, the module shall:

- Drive all outputs to a safe, known, inactive state.
- Deassert all class interrupt outputs.
- Deassert all escalation outputs.
- Present valid inactive differential signaling states on alert and escalation interfaces.
- Set all configuration registers to their reset values.
- Disable all alert source enables and all local alert enables.
- Disable all escalation behavior.
- Not perform liveness checks.
- Not assert any interrupt as a result of power-up or reset conditions.

Until software locks configuration, alert events shall not be interpreted as actionable interrupts unless the associated alert source has been explicitly enabled and classified.

## 3. Bus Interface and Register Behavior

The module shall behave as a slave peripheral on the system bus. It shall support software reads and writes to its register space.

The module shall provide registers or register fields for:

- Enabling and disabling each alert source.
- Enabling and disabling each local alert.
- Assigning each alert source to a class.
- Assigning each local alert to a class.
- Programming alert accumulation thresholds.
- Programming interrupt timeout values.
- Programming escalation phase durations.
- Programming escalation severity enables and phase mappings.
- Reading and clearing accumulated counts.
- Reading and clearing escalation state and counts.
- Reading alert cause and local alert cause status.
- Reading and clearing class interrupt status.
- Triggering class interrupts by software.
- Locking the configuration.

Sticky status and cause bits shall remain asserted until explicitly cleared by software. Clearing is performed by software writes to the corresponding status or cause fields.

Once configuration has been locked, all configuration fields that were included in the lock shall become read-only until the next system reset. A locked configuration shall not be modifiable through any write to the bus interface.

Software-triggered interrupt test writes shall assert the corresponding class interrupt output. Such test writes shall not increment the associated class accumulation counter.

## 4. Alert Event Handling

Each external alert source presents a differential message interface. The module shall detect native alert events and liveness responses from each source, and shall provide acknowledgment and liveness-request signaling back to the source.

When an enabled alert source asserts a native alert event:

- The module shall record which source caused the event by setting the corresponding sticky cause bit.
- The module shall attribute the event to the configured class for that source.
- The module shall assert the interrupt output for that class.
- The module shall increment the accumulation counter for that class as described in the escalation behavior section.
- The module shall start or restart the interrupt timeout for that class if a nonzero timeout is configured and class escalation is enabled.

When an alert source is disabled, events from that source shall be ignored for the purposes of cause recording, interrupt assertion, accumulation, and escalation triggering.

If multiple enabled alert events assigned to the same class occur in the same cycle, the class accumulation counter shall advance by at most one for that cycle. The module shall not count simultaneous events in the same class individually.

A native alert event that occurs while a liveness check is in progress shall not be lost. The module shall preserve the event and deliver it after the liveness transaction has completed.

## 5. Local Alerts

The module shall generate four internal local alert events:

1. Failure of an alert-source liveness check.
2. Failure of an escalation-path liveness check.
3. Invalid signaling or missing acknowledgment on an enabled alert-source interface.
4. Invalid signaling or missing response on an escalation output interface.

Each local alert shall have its own enable bit, class assignment, cause bit, and interrupt behavior. A local alert that is disabled shall not set a cause bit, shall not assert a class interrupt, and shall not contribute to class accumulation or escalation.

For alert-source signal integrity failures, only failures on interfaces whose corresponding alert source is enabled shall be treated as local alert events. Failures on disabled alert-source interfaces shall be ignored.

Escalation-path signal integrity failures shall contribute to the escalation signal-integrity local alert unless that local alert is itself disabled.

## 6. Liveness Checking

After configuration is locked, the module shall begin periodic liveness checks on alert and escalation signaling paths.

The module shall:

- Randomize the interval between liveness checks.
- Randomize the selection of the path to check.
- Use the entropy input to perturb the randomization sequence when valid entropy is present.
- Continue to operate correctly if the entropy input is tied to a constant value, though with reduced randomization.
- Select only enabled alert-source interfaces for alert liveness checks.
- Select all implemented escalation interfaces for escalation liveness checks.
- Check one path at a time.

When a liveness check is issued, the module shall wait for a valid response. If the response arrives before the programmable liveness timeout, the check shall be considered successful.

If no valid response arrives before the timeout, the module shall:

- Raise the corresponding liveness-failure local alert.
- End the current liveness check.
- Proceed to the next scheduled liveness check.

If a liveness response arrives when no liveness request is pending, the module shall treat this as a liveness-failure local alert.

## 7. Interrupt Behavior

The module shall provide one interrupt output per class.

The class interrupt output shall be asserted whenever the corresponding class interrupt status is set. It shall remain asserted until software clears that status.

A class interrupt status shall be set when:

- An enabled alert source assigned to that class asserts a native alert event.
- An enabled local alert assigned to that class is raised.
- Software writes to the corresponding interrupt test field.

The class interrupt shall be independent of whether class escalation is enabled. Disabling class escalation shall not prevent interrupt assertion.

Clearing a class interrupt status shall also stop and clear any active interrupt timeout for that class.

The module shall expose interrupt state so software can determine which class asserted an interrupt and which cause bits were set.

## 8. Accumulation and Escalation Triggering

Each class shall have an accumulation counter and a programmable accumulation threshold.

The accumulation counter shall:

- Increment when one or more enabled class-alert events occur in a cycle.
- Saturate at its maximum representable value.
- Not wrap around.
- Be readable by software.
- Be clearable by software, subject to escalation locking rules.

The accumulation threshold shall determine when escalation is triggered for that class:

- If the threshold is zero, the first counted event shall trigger escalation.
- If the threshold is T, escalation shall be triggered on the (T+1)-th counted event.

Escalation triggering is enabled only if the corresponding class escalation enable is set.

The module shall also trigger escalation for a class if:

- The class interrupt remains asserted,
- A nonzero interrupt timeout is configured,
- Class escalation is enabled,
- The interrupt is not cleared before the timeout expires.

In this case, the timeout mechanism shall start when the class interrupt is asserted and shall be canceled when the interrupt is cleared.

If class escalation is disabled, the accumulation counter shall not advance and the interrupt timeout shall not operate.

## 9. Escalation Protocol

When escalation is triggered for a class, the class shall enter an escalation sequence. The sequence shall progress through up to four phases, numbered 0 through 3.

Each phase shall have a programmable duration. A phase shall last at least one clock cycle even if its programmed duration is zero.

Each escalation severity output shall have:

- A programmable enable.
- A programmable mapping to one of the four escalation phases.

During a given escalation phase, the module shall assert every escalation severity output whose enable is set and whose mapping selects that phase. Severity outputs mapped to other phases shall not be asserted during that phase.

Unless the class escalation has been locked against clearing, software may abort an active escalation by writing the class clear control. A class clear shall:

- Clear the class accumulation counter.
- Return the class escalation state machine to idle.
- Not clear the class interrupt status.

If the class escalation lock is set, software clearing shall have no effect on an active escalation once escalation has begun.

After the escalation sequence has completed all programmed phases, the class shall enter a terminal escalation state. The class shall remain in this state until reset or until software is permitted to clear escalation and performs the clear operation.

## 10. Escalation Output Signaling and Monitoring

Each escalation severity output shall use differential signaling. The module shall drive valid differential states when an escalation severity is asserted and when it is inactive.

The module shall monitor the escalation signaling path for each severity output.

If an escalation output is asserted and the corresponding response is missing, invalid, or not maintained, the module shall raise the escalation signal-integrity local alert.

If a differential encoding error is present on an escalation interface, the module shall raise the escalation signal-integrity local alert.

Liveness checks on escalation paths shall not be interpreted as escalation requests. A successful liveness response shall not assert an escalation output.

## 11. Crashdump Output

The module shall provide a crashdump output that carries a snapshot of selected status and state information.

The crashdump output shall:

- Be valid and known after reset.
- Reflect current configuration, cause, interrupt, accumulation, and escalation state.
- Be updated as the module state changes.
- Be readable by hardware debug logic without requiring bus access.

The crashdump output shall not alter module behavior when read or observed.

## 12. Global Behavioral Constraints

The module shall never generate an interrupt or escalation as a result of reset alone.

The module shall never modify locked configuration fields through any internal event.

The module shall tolerate a constant entropy input and remain functionally correct.

The module shall keep all outputs in a known, safe, inactive state whenever the system is in reset.

The module shall support the configured number of alert sources while maintaining the behavioral requirements described in this specification.

# Behavioral Specification: Alert Accumulator

## Overview

This module implements a saturating accumulation counter for alert events belonging to one alert class. It counts enabled alert occurrences, compares the current count against a programmable threshold, and produces an escalation trigger indication only when a new enabled occurrence arrives after the count has already reached or exceeded that threshold.

The accumulator does not wrap around. It saturates at its maximum representable count and remains there until explicitly cleared or reset.

## Reset and Initialization

- On reset, the accumulated count shall become zero.
- Reset shall override all other input conditions.
- The count output shall present the current accumulated count.

## Counting Behavior

- The module counts at most one occurrence per clock cycle.
- When a trigger occurrence is present and the class is enabled:
  - If the current count is below its maximum value, the count shall increment by one.
  - If the current count is already at its maximum value, the count shall remain at that maximum value.
- When no trigger occurrence is present, or when the class is disabled, the count shall not change.
- A disabled class shall not accumulate missed triggers. Triggers that arrive while the class is disabled shall be ignored.
- The count shall continue to increment on subsequent enabled triggers after the threshold has been reached, until it saturates.

## Clear Behavior

- When a clear request is asserted, the count shall become zero on the next active clock edge.
- Clear shall take priority over any increment caused by a trigger.
- Clear shall be effective regardless of whether the class is enabled or disabled.
- If clear remains asserted, the count shall remain zero.
- Asserting clear shall not, by itself, cause the escalation trigger output to be asserted.

## Escalation Trigger Output

The escalation trigger output shall be asserted only when **all** of the following conditions are true in the same cycle:

1. The class is enabled.
2. A trigger occurrence is present.
3. The current count, before applying the current trigger, is greater than or equal to the configured threshold.

In all other cases, the escalation trigger output shall be deasserted.

In particular:

- Reaching or exceeding the threshold is not enough by itself to assert the output. A trigger occurrence must also be present.
- If the current count is below the threshold, an enabled trigger shall not assert the output, even if that trigger causes the count to reach the threshold.
- If the current count is at or above the threshold, every subsequent enabled trigger shall assert the output.
- The trigger output shall not be latched. It shall be asserted only while the qualifying conditions are satisfied.
- Asserting the trigger output shall not clear the accumulator or stop it from counting.

## Threshold Semantics

The threshold comparison uses the accumulator value at the start of the cycle, before any update from the current trigger is applied.

Therefore:

- If the threshold is zero, the first enabled trigger shall assert the escalation trigger output, because the current count is always greater than or equal to zero.
- If the threshold is set to a nonzero value N, the first enabled trigger that arrives after the count has reached N shall assert the output. Starting from zero, this is the (N+1)-th enabled trigger if no clear or reset occurs in between.

## Saturation and Maximum Count

- The count shall saturate at the maximum value representable by its configured width.
- Once saturated, additional enabled triggers shall not change the count.
- A saturated count shall still satisfy the threshold comparison, and an enabled trigger at saturation shall assert the escalation trigger output if the threshold has been reached.

## Simultaneous Clear and Trigger

If a clear request and an enabled trigger occur in the same cycle:

- Clear shall take priority for the next accumulator state; the count shall become zero on the next active clock edge.
- The escalation trigger output for that cycle shall still be evaluated using the count value before the clear. If that pre-clear count is at or above the threshold, the output shall assert.
- The clear shall not retroactively suppress the trigger output for that cycle.

## Summary of Required Behavior

| Condition | Next Count | Trigger Output |
|---|---|---|
| Reset asserted | Zero | Does not depend on the count |
| Clear asserted | Zero | Depends on trigger/enable/count conditions |
| Class disabled, no clear | Unchanged | Deasserted |
| Class disabled, clear asserted | Zero | Deasserted |
| Class enabled, no trigger, no clear | Unchanged | Deasserted |
| Class enabled, trigger present, count below threshold, no clear | Increment unless saturated | Deasserted |
| Class enabled, trigger present, count at/above threshold, no clear | Increment unless saturated | Asserted |
| Trigger present while saturated | Stay at maximum | Asserted if count is at/above threshold |

The module shall maintain this behavior for all valid input combinations and shall never wrap from its maximum count to zero except through reset or an explicit clear.

# Behavioral Specification for the Alert Classification Module

## Overview

This module is a combinational gating and classification function for security alert events. It receives alert trigger indications, per-alert enable controls, and per-alert class assignments. It produces:

- a per-alert cause indication for each alert source,
- a per-alert cause indication for each locally generated alert source, and
- one class trigger output for each of the four supported alert classes.

The module does not store state, accumulate events, generate interrupts, or perform escalation. Its outputs reflect the current input conditions continuously.

## Functional Requirements

### Per-Alert Cause Generation

For every alert source and every local alert source, the module must assert that source’s cause output only when both of the following conditions are true:

- the source’s trigger indication is active, and
- the source’s enable indication is active.

If either condition is false, the cause output for that source must be deasserted.

The cause output for a source must not depend on the source’s class assignment. Whether an alert is assigned to class A, B, C, or D, its cause output must behave identically.

Cause outputs are not sticky and are not latched. They must follow the current state of the trigger and enable inputs.

### Alert Classification

Each alert source and each local alert source must be assigned to exactly one of the four classes.

For each class, the class trigger output must be asserted whenever at least one enabled alert source assigned to that class has an active trigger indication. This includes both regular alert sources and local alert sources.

The module must treat local alert sources the same as regular alert sources for the purpose of class trigger generation. An active local alert assigned to a class must contribute to that class’s trigger output in the same manner as a regular alert.

An alert source whose enable is deasserted must not contribute to any class trigger output, even if its trigger indication is active.

If multiple enabled alert sources assigned to the same class are active simultaneously, the class trigger output must remain asserted. There is no priority between sources and no exclusion between them.

The class trigger output must remain asserted only while at least one contributing enabled alert remains active. When all contributing alert causes for that class are deasserted, the class trigger output must deassert.

If a source’s class assignment changes while its cause is active, the class trigger output of the previously assigned class must deassert, and the class trigger output of the newly assigned class must assert, provided the source remains enabled.

### Independence of Outputs

Each cause output must be independent of all other cause outputs. An event on one alert source must not cause a cause output for another source to assert.

The four class trigger outputs are independent. Assertion of one class trigger output must not imply assertion of any other class trigger output unless there are separately enabled active alert sources assigned to that other class.

### Behavioral Characteristics

The module is purely combinational. It has no clock, no reset, and no internal state. All outputs must follow changes on the enable, trigger, and class assignment inputs without requiring software action, initialization, or configuration.
